name: @arthome/contracts
description: Arthome boundary contracts: the DTO schemas the BFFs serve and accept, derived from @arthome/core and never redeclared.
_comment_exports: NO "." ENTRY POINT, AND THAT IS THE BARREL RULE MADE STRUCTURAL.
D-012 forbids a barrel here, measured: zod's classic entry made 64 translation
files reachable — 93 KB gzip against 7.5 KB — at a cost that is FIXED and tied
to the import rather than marginal and tied to the number of schemas. A barrel
defeats tree-shaking on any bundler without cross-module analysis, which
includes Metro by default.
⚠ AND QUOTE THE THIRD NUMBER OR NONE OF THEM. With tree shaking OFF, zod/mini
measures 85 KB — the classic entry's level. So the saving is not reduced when
Metro declines to tree-shake, it is ZERO, and 93-against-7.5 on its own sells
a gain nobody has yet been shown to collect. The rule below survives that
intact, because it rests on the cost being fixed and tied to the import.
A written rule against barrels would be a rule someone breaks in a hurry. With
no "." export, `import { X } from '@arthome/contracts'` fails to RESOLVE — the
same trick @arthome/tooling uses to stay out of production. The constraint is
the mechanism, not a convention.
So one subpath per bounded context, added as each lands, never before: a
subpath in `exports` that points at a file which does not exist is unreachable
with a laconic error, and a subpath missing from `exports` is unreachable too.
Both are silent, so the list stays honest rather than aspirational.
./identity  ./catalog  ./ticketing  ./chat  ./payouts  ./streaming
./notifications                        — one per service
./envelope                             — the shared response and error envelope
See architecture/code-conventions.md section 5.5 and DECISIONS.md D-012.
_comment_peer: BOTH DEPENDENCIES ARE PEERS, EXACTLY PINNED, AND THE TEST DECIDES IT RATHER
THAN CONVENIENCE.
The question from code-conventions.md 4.2 is: does the consuming repository
name this package itself? For both of these it does — a surface imports
@arthome/core for the rules and zod for its own validation — and the regime-A
membership test then applies: if two copies exist at once, does something break
at runtime in a way that is hard to diagnose?
zod            yes. Two copies is two schema registries and unintelligible
validation errors. Regime A of versions.json.
@arthome/core  yes, and this one is easy to miss. Two copies means two sets
of `as const` vocabulary constants, so `mode === ChatMode.OPEN`
is false against the other copy's constant — the silent
equality failure that D-038 and D-033 both are, arriving
through the dependency graph instead of through a spelling.
A regular dependency would let pnpm install a second copy beside the app's own.
Declared as peers, there is exactly one of each and the consumer owns it.
And both are ALSO pinned in devDependencies, which is not redundant: a package
that declares a peer without pinning it for itself gets an auto-installed peer
at the LOWEST member of the range. That is how @arthome/tooling ended up
resolving eslint 9.39.5 while the root had 10.11.0 — two copies, both working,
differently, nothing red.
